note: Ha'asherot are the goddess Asherah (plural, local forms) or her wooden cult poles; the KJV, following the LXX/Vulgate "groves", turns a deity into trees.

mine: a man restricted in his right hand
note: 'Itter yad-yemino is literally "bound/impeded as to his right hand"; it may mean a disability or a trained left-hander (cf. 20:16), and the narrative turns on his hiding the sword on the unexpected side.
Gomed occurs only here; it is an unknown, probably shorter measure (LXX "a span"), not the usual 'ammah "cubit".
Pesilim everywhere else means carved idols or images; "quarries" is a guess from the root "to hew". Same in v.26.

kjv: so that he (Ehud) could not draw the dagger out
mine: for he (Ehud) did not draw the sword out
note: Ki lo' shalaf states that Ehud did not pull it out (deliberately leaving it), not that he was unable to.
Happarshedonah is a hapax; it may mean faeces (the bowel contents) or an exit, "he went out to the vestibule"; the KJV and I take the first sense.
Mesik 'et-raglaw "covering his feet" is a euphemism for defecating (cf. 1 Sam 24:3); the literal KJV hides the point of the servants' delay.
Shamen "fat, robust" means stout, vigorous men; "lusty" now suggests sexual desire.
